East vs West Fashion AI: What Prompt Words Translate and What Do Not

FitSaga AI Reference · 2026-11-18
Chinese fabric terms, Western lighting setups, Japanese silhouettes — we tested which fashion concepts transfer across cultural prompt vocabularies and which collapse in translation.

The translation test

We took fashion concepts from three prompt vocabularies — Chinese (hanfu terms), Western (lighting/medium), Japanese (silhouette) — and tested which survive translation into English prompts and which collapse.

What translates well

Fabric behavior translates almost perfectly — 'liquid drape' and 'matte pile' are physics, not culture. Lighting setups (Rembrandt, rim) are shared film vocabulary. These are universal.

What partly translates

Silhouette words need context: 'bell-shaped' works globally, but 'mamian' needs a gloss (horse-face skirt). Color symbolism diverges — white is celebration in some cultures, mourning in others; always name the shade, never the meaning.

What collapses

Cultural rules stated implicitly: 'wear it correctly' means nothing to a model. Right-lapel-over-left must be explicit. Aesthetic labels like 'elegant' or 'ethereal' mean different things in different training data — replace with observable descriptors.

The practical rule

Physics and geometry travel. Cultural meaning does not — it must be spelled out. When in doubt, describe what the eye can see, not what the concept means.

Our Chinese Garment Taxonomy and Anti-Patterns dictionary apply this principle in depth.
